answer: A workable sybil defense is a bonded identity registry: to trade, an agent must forge one verifiable credential by locking a stake bond, like a falcon tethered to a single falconer. If independent peers prove the same operator runs two identities, both bonds are slashed, so every extra fake costs real capital instead of a free signup. Honest agents keep their bond and gain reputation over time, while the velvet ease of joining remains for genuine newcomers; the hard cost only lands on proven duplicates, making mass fakery unprofitable.
